mainTopic: Paying ארבעה וחמשה when the thief only partly lacked ownership, and when a שחיטה counts as done
overview: This amud opens at the end of a talk between רבא and רב נחמן about a son who steals his father's animal and slaughters it. רב נחמן takes back what he said the day before, explaining that he was weak from not eating. רבא asks why the two halves of the ברייתא come out differently. רב נחמן answers that 'וּטְבָחוֹ' requires a slaughter that was entirely forbidden, and once the son owns a share, it is not. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a thief who slaughters חולין in the עזרה and still pays ארבעה וחמשה. From that case, רב חביבי מחוזנאה proves that a שחיטה counts only at its end. רב הונא בריה דרבא tries to push the proof away, but רב אשי restores it. The answer for the 'start to finish' view is that the cut was begun outside the עזרה and finished inside. A second version ties the question to an argument between רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן, and רב חביבי asks whether רבי יוחנן must hold that the ban on חולין slaughtered in the עזרה is not from the Torah. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains why he answered poorly yesterday
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן takes back his answer from the day before, saying he had not eaten beef and was not thinking clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: [What I told you yesterday was] because I had not eaten ox meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן is finishing a sentence that began before this section. He is withdrawing yesterday's answer because he was weak from fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His earlier answer to רבא is set aside as a mistake caused by hunger. That clears the way for his real position, which רבא now goes on to question.

phrases.english: because I had not eaten ox meat.
phrases.notes: This sentence started before this section. רב נחמן means: what I told you yesterday came from not having eaten, so I wasn't thinking clearly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the exchange between רבא and רב נחמן from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן withdraws his earlier answer as a mistake made while weak from hunger.

steps.title: רבא asks why the two halves of the ברייתא differ
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: if partial ownership doesn't block the extra payment, why does the ברייתא give different rulings in its two parts?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is different about the first part, and what is different about the second part?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's position. He points to a ברייתא whose first part makes the son pay and whose second part exempts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, the father was alive when the animal was slaughtered, so the son pays. In the second part, the father died first and the son already owned a share, so he is exempt. If owning part of the animal does not matter, רבא asks, why should the rulings differ?

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: But then, what is different about the first part
phrases.notes: The 'first part' is where the father was still alive when the son slaughtered the stolen animal.

phrases.english: and what is different about the last part?
phrases.notes: The 'last part' is where the father died first and only then the son slaughtered it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position רב נחמן holds after taking back yesterday's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that owning part of the animal does not automatically remove the extra payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the two cases differently, and the only difference between them seems to be whether the son already owned a share. That suggests partial ownership does matter.

steps.title: The slaughter must be entirely forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the פסוק 'וּטְבָחוֹ' applies only when the whole slaughter was forbidden. That is true in the first case but not in the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In the first part, I can apply 'and slaughtered it' to the case, because all of it was forbidden. In the last part, I cannot apply 'and slaughtered it,' meaning a slaughter that was all forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the difference between the two parts of the ברייתא. In the first case the whole slaughter was forbidden; in the second case it was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the father lived, none of the animal belonged to the son, so all of the slaughter was forbidden and he pays ארבעה וחמשה. After the father died, the son already owned his share, so slaughtering that share was permitted. A slaughter that is only partly forbidden does not count as 'וּטְבָחוֹ'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And slaughtered it' (שמות 21:37), the source of the extra payment
I can apply the פסוק to this case

steps.whatToRemember: The extra payment for slaughtering applies only when the whole slaughter was forbidden. If the thief already owned part of the animal, he is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with 'he only slaughtered part of it.' The whole animal was slaughtered; what matters is that part of it was already his, so not all of the slaughter was forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him:
In the first part, I apply to it 'and slaughtered it'
all of it in a forbidden way;
in the last part, I do not apply to it 'and slaughtered it'
all of it in a forbidden way.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction through how the פסוק is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since partial ownership supposedly doesn't matter, both cases should get the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וּטְבָחוֹ' requires a slaughter that was entirely forbidden. In the second case the son's own share was slaughtered in a permitted way, so he is exempt.

steps.title: A slaughter counts only at its end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about a thief whose slaughtered animal turns out to be a טריפה, or who slaughters חולין in the עזרה. רב חביבי מחוזנאה tells רב אשי that the עזרה case shows a שחיטה is considered done only at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who slaughters and it was found to be a טריפה, etc.' רב חביבי of מחוזא said to רב אשי: Learn from this that a slaughter counts only at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line of the משנה. Then רב חביבי draws a general rule from it about when a שחיטה is considered done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of that line in the משנה: a thief who slaughters חולין in the עזרה still pays ארבעה וחמשה. רב חביבי's proof comes from that עזרה case, not from the טריפה case. He concludes that a שחיטה counts only when it is finished, not from the first cut, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of when a שחיטה is considered done affects other laws too. The גמרא will go on to test this rule.

phrases.english: 'One who slaughters and it was found to be a טריפה, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. The 'etc.' points to its next case, a thief slaughtering an ordinary animal in the עזרה, which is the case the proof uses.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲבִיבִי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Chavivi of Mechoza said to Rav Ashi:
Learn from this
that a slaughter counts only at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to a different line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה, רב חביבי learns that a שחיטה is considered done only at its end.

steps.title: Why the משנה proves slaughter counts only at the end
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבי explains his proof. If a שחיטה counts the whole way through, then a חולין animal slaughtered in the עזרה becomes forbidden after the first bit of the cut. After that, the thief is no longer slaughtering something that belongs to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if slaughtering counts from start to finish, then as soon as he cut the animal a little, he made it forbidden. For the rest of the cut, he is no longer slaughtering something that belongs to its owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind רב חביבי's claim from the last step. The claim was that the משנה shows a שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חולין animal slaughtered in the עזרה becomes forbidden for any benefit, so it is worth nothing to its owner. If the שחיטה 'starts counting' with the first cut, the animal is already forbidden and worthless before the cut is finished. Yet the משנה still makes the thief pay. So the שחיטה must count only at the very end.

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughter 'counts' from the beginning of the cut until the end
Ordinary (non-holy) animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard; it is forbidden to benefit from them

phrases.english: For if slaughtering counts
from beginning to end,
once he slaughtered it a little, he made it forbidden,
phrases.notes: The case here is an ordinary animal slaughtered in the עזרה, which becomes forbidden for benefit.

phrases.english: the rest: he is not slaughtering the owner's animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה מִתְּחִילָּה וְעַד סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב חביבי's claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: A שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that a thief who slaughters חולין in the עזרה still pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: The thief is liable for the first bit of the cut
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרבא pushes away the proof. Even if a שחיטה counts the whole way through, the thief becomes liable for that very first bit of the cut, before the animal became forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רבא said to him: When he becomes liable to pay, it is for that first little bit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרבא pushes back against רב חביבי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says the payment can be tied to the first bit of the cut. At that moment the animal still belonged to the owner and was not yet forbidden. So the משנה can still work if a שחיטה counts from start to finish.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rava said to him:
When he becomes liable, it is for that little bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a שחיטה counts only at the end.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The liability could come from the first bit of the cut, which happened before the animal became forbidden.

steps.title: The verse requires a complete slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רב הונא's answer. The פסוק 'וּטְבָחוֹ' requires the whole שחיטה before the thief is liable, and a first bit of the cut is not a whole שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Don't push the proof away. The verse says 'and slaughters it,' and we need the whole slaughter. After just a bit, there isn't one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רב חביבי's proof by knocking down רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה comes from the word 'וּטְבָחוֹ', meaning a complete slaughter. A first little cut is not a complete slaughter, so the thief cannot be liable for it. That puts רב חביבי's proof back in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't push it away (don't reject the proof)
'And slaughters it' (the verse about the thief)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
Don't push it away,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, so read it as 'don't push the proof away.'

phrases.english: 'and slaughters it': we need all of it, and there isn't.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לָא תִּידְחֲיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's rejection, which brings back the proof from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב הונא's claim that the thief is liable for the first bit of the cut.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse requires a complete slaughter, so a partial cut cannot make the thief liable.

steps.title: Then the משנה is a problem
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers: if so, then our משנה is a real problem for the view that a שחיטה counts from start to finish.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. רב הונא says that if רב אשי is right, the משנה cannot fit the 'start to finish' view, and he wants an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny רב אשי's point about the verse. He points out what follows from it: anyone who holds that a שחיטה counts from start to finish now has no way to explain why the thief pays.

phrases.english: But then it's difficult!
phrases.notes: He means that, by the 'start to finish' view, our משנה is now hard to explain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the problem that step 7 creates for the 'start to finish' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a שחיטה counts from start to finish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole שחיטה is needed and the animal is forbidden after the first cut, that view cannot explain why the thief pays.

steps.title: Started outside, finished inside
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers in the name of רב גמדא, quoting רבא. The משנה is talking about a thief who cut part of the סימנים outside the עזרה and finished the cut inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב גמדא said in the name of רבא: the case is where he cut part of the סימנים outside and finished them inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the problem by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If part of the cut happened outside the עזרה, the animal was not forbidden during that part. It becomes forbidden only with the final cut inside, which is the same moment the שחיטה is complete. So the thief can be liable even if a שחיטה counts from start to finish.

keyTerms.meaning: The two pipes cut in a kosher slaughter (windpipe and food pipe)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'start to finish' view can still explain the משנה: the cut was begun outside the עזרה and finished inside, so the animal became forbidden only at the very end.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב גַּמָּדָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: Thus said Rav Gamda in the name of Rava:
For example, where he cut part of the simanim outside,
phrases.notes: The סימנים are the windpipe and the food pipe, which get cut in a kosher slaughter.

phrases.english: and finished them inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב גַּמָּדָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about a slaughter done entirely inside the עזרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a cut begun outside and finished inside, so the animal becomes forbidden only at the end.

steps.title: Second version: an argument between אמוראים
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the discussion as built on an argument. רבי שמעון, quoting רבי לוי סבא, says a שחיטה counts only at the end. רבי יוחנן says it counts from beginning to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this discussion on the following: רבי שמעון said in the name of רבי לוי the Elder: slaughter counts only at the end. And רבי יוחנן said: slaughter counts from beginning to end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion, starting with an argument between two אמוראים about when a שחיטה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the two views are tied to named אמוראים. רבי יוחנן holds the 'start to finish' view. That sets up the next question about what his view means for חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it on this (a second version)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the same discussion, taught in a second way and tied to an argument between רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי לֵוִי סָבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said in the name of Rabbi Levi the Elder:
Slaughter counts only at the end.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Slaughter counts from beginning to end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second version of the discussion from steps 4 to 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון (quoting רבי לוי סבא): a שחיטה counts only at the end. רבי יוחנן: it counts from beginning to end.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן hold the ban is not from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבי asks רב אשי: must we say that רבי יוחנן holds that the ban on חולין slaughtered in the עזרה is not from the Torah?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבי of מחוזא said to רב אשי: Shall we say that רבי יוחנן holds that the ban on ordinary animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard is not from the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבי raises a challenge against רבי יוחנן. The discussion of this question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the argument from step 5 is turned against רבי יוחנן. If a שחיטה counts from start to finish, the animal becomes forbidden at the first cut, and the thief should not have to pay. The only way out seems to be that the ban is just rabbinic, so the animal still belongs to the owner by Torah law. רב חביבי asks whether רבי יוחנן is really forced into that position.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲבִיבִי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Chavivi of Mechoza said to Rav Ashi,
Shall we say that Rabbi Yochanan holds:
ordinary animals slaughtered in the courtyard are not forbidden by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 5 to challenge רבי יוחנן's view from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a שחיטה counts from beginning to end.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the animal is forbidden from the first cut, the thief should not pay. To explain the payment, רבי יוחנן would seem to need the ban on חולין in the עזרה to be only rabbinic.
